items.title: Pay demanded 'data protection registration' fee
items.quote: Zahlen Sie die Gebühr bis zum 29.07.2026 auf das Konto IBAN LT21 7044 0000 0447 1229 (Empfänger: Registerservice M. Kovalenko).
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date for payment ('bis zum 29.07.2026'), which is used as written without recalculation. No weekend/holiday adjustment is needed since it is a specific date, not a counted period. Note: this falls well before today's date (2026-10-01), so even taken at face value the stated deadline has already passed.

warnings: This strongly resembles a well-known German scam pattern: a private company (often based abroad) sends an unsolicited 'Gebührenbescheid' falsely claiming that Art. 30 DSGVO requires paid registration in a 'central Datenschutzregister' — no such mandatory paid register exists; Art. 30 GDPR only requires companies to keep their own internal processing records, free of charge.
The sender is a private Lithuanian limited company (UAB), not a German or EU data-protection authority, despite the official-sounding name 'DSR Datenschutz-Registerstelle Europa' and letterhead.

The payment recipient name on the IBAN ('Registerservice M. Kovalenko') does not match the sender's name on the letterhead ('DSR Datenschutz-Registerstelle Europa UAB') — a classic red flag for fraudulent invoices.
The IBAN is a foreign (Lithuanian) account, unusual and suspicious for a supposed EU/German regulatory fee.
The letter uses pressure tactics: a very short payment deadline (one week from the document date) and a threat of disproportionate fines up to €20,000,000 for non-payment.

The letter explicitly denies any right to object ('Ein Widerspruch gegen die Erfassung ist nicht möglich') and restricts queries to email only, which is atypical for a genuine authority and designed to prevent verification or recourse.

Recommendation: do not pay this invoice and do not reply; verify independently with a real data protection authority (e.g. the Landesbeauftragte für Datenschutz) and consider reporting it as fraud/phishing.

By the time this letter is being reviewed (today 2026-10-01), the stated payment deadline of 29.07.2026 has already passed, which is itself inconsistent with it being a serious, actively enforced demand.
